claims.claim: Nutrien reported record first-half potash sales volumes and production while progressing mine automation and keeping controllable potash cash cost below $60 per tonne, reinforcing its role in scaled crop-input supply.

risks.risk: Fertilizer economics remain exposed to commodity benchmarks, natural-gas costs, weather, farmer affordability and geopolitics.

unknowns.unknown: Long-run automation productivity and normalized potash pricing need separate underwriting.

claims.claim: Nutrien reported Q2 net earnings of $1.22 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $2.43 billion; first-half operating cash flow rose 12%, while management raised potash sales-volume guidance and lowered capital-expenditure guidance ranges.

risks.risk: Strong results partly reflect higher global fertilizer benchmarks, which are cyclical and not wholly execution-driven.

unknowns.unknown: Normalized through-cycle earnings power requires commodity-price sensitivity analysis.
